title: Grill — Pipeline Human Step
summary:
Before Planning: **12 decisions** that change the shape of the build, plus a **confirm list** of defaults (one click each). The first four decide what the user sees and how the run state machine behaves; the next three decide what Return actually does; then the panel, escape hatches, CLI and the bundle contract.

The investigation found **no existing human-step code** and all baseline suites green. The load-bearing gaps are: the Review card's Done button 409s for a non-done pipeline; there is no `review` run status; the previous step can walk away from the gate after a return; and a human gate has no task row, so the run view and attention resolver cannot see it.

Source: the pipeline step task text (no PRD in the repo), grounded in `docs/plans/pipeline-human-step-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **No human-step code exists today, and the pipeline baseline is green.** `bun test` on the five pipeline suites: 239 + 184 + 114 + 73 + 208 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` clean. Everything below is additive.

**The graph validator strips an unknown `type` and currently accepts an agent-less start step.** A read-only probe of a one-step `{type:"human"}` graph returned `ok:true`; `newStep()` emits no `type` field.

evidence.label: newStep emits no type

proven.text: **`createTask`, `buildSnapshot` and `launchStep` all reject a step with no agent.** A human step must be exempted in all three, or it can never be created, snapshotted or launched.

evidence.label: createTask rejects a no-agent step
buildSnapshot rejects a no-agent step
launchStep blocks with profile-missing

proven.text: **A Review-column pipeline parent's Done button 409s today.** The card renders Done for any `column === "review"`, but the server only allows `column:"done"` when `pipelineRun.status === "done"`.

evidence.label: card renders Done for any Review card
server only allows done → Done

proven.text: **A human gate has no task row, so today's run view and attention resolver cannot see it.** `reviewActive` only walks `run.active` and looks up a step task; `pipelineAttentionStepTask` also resolves step tasks only. The human panel must key off the new run state.

evidence.label: reviewActive only sees task-backed executions

proven.text: **A plain Run on a `review` run would silently restart it.** `startPipelineRun` only special-cases `blocked`/`cancelled` (retry) and `done` (refuse); every other status falls through to the fresh-run path, discarding history and the gate.

evidence.label: no guard for a new status

proven.text: **No SQL migration is needed.** `pipelines.graph` and `tasks.pipeline_run` are JSON columns; old steps default to agent and old runs default to no human gates.

evidence.label: run state is JSON on the task

sections.title: Run state & the card
sections.intro: These decide what the owner sees when the pipeline reaches the gate, and how the run's status machine changes.

questions.title: When a human step is pending in the Review column, what should the board card offer?
questions.why: Sets the card's primary/secondary actions, the context menu, and the server's column guard. The wrong choice leaves a Done button that 409s or makes the gate amber, contradicting "same as Review".
questions.context: Today every `column:"review"` card renders **Done**, but the server only accepts `column:"done"` when `pipelineRun.status === "done"`; a pipeline parent's column is otherwise managed by its run. The card shows **Open** once `pipelineRun.history.length > 0`. So a human gate in Review would show a Done button that 409s unless the card, the menu and the guard change.

evidence.label: card renders Done for any review card
server guard
evidence.code:
const parkingFinished = before.pipelineRun?.status === "done" && patch.column === "done";
if (!parkingFinished) return json({ error: "pipeline task's column is managed by its run" }, { status: 409, ... });

evidence.label: Open once any step has run
evidence.code:
const hasOpenablePipelineRun = !!task.pipelineRun && task.pipelineRun.history.length > 0;
const openable = task.hasOpenableRun || hasOpenablePipelineRun;

options.label: Open + Review (Done suppressed)
options.description: The card reads like Review: neutral Open, plus a neutral **Review** button that opens the human panel. Done is hidden until the gate is accepted and the run is done.
options.consequence: TaskCard + context menu + the PATCH guard all change; the card matches Review without an amber ring.

options.label: Review only (Done suppressed)
options.description: Review is the primary action; Open stays reachable from inside the panel/run view.
options.consequence: Fewer buttons, but the user loses the direct transcript entry point on the card.

options.label: Open only (the panel lives inside the run view)
options.description: No new card action; the user opens the run view and clicks the highlighted gate node.
options.consequence: Least card wiring, but the gate is one click deeper and easier to miss.

options.label: Keep Done, repurposed as terminal Accept
options.description: Done only on a gate with no outgoing edge; it accepts and finishes. Hidden when there is a next step.
options.consequence: Overloads Done and drops Return from the card; the server/Done plumbing gets more special cases.

recommendation.reason: Keeps the card visually identical to Review while making the gate one click away; Done is only valid after a terminal Accept makes the run done.

questions.title: Represent the pause as a new `review` run status, or reuse `blocked` / `running`?
questions.why: Every exhaustive status map, `deriveRunStatus`, the sanitizer, the board column mapping, the CLI/TUI and the notifications depend on this.
questions.context: `PipelineRunStatus` is `idle | running | blocked | done | cancelled`. `persist` maps `done → review`, so Review is currently a terminal-only column. `deriveRunStatus` is blocked > cancelled > running > done. A `review` status is non-terminal: no `endedAt`, no Done button, no "Pipeline finished" toast.

evidence.label: the status union
evidence.code: export type PipelineRunStatus = "idle" | "running" | "blocked" | "done" | "cancelled";

evidence.label: column mapping
status derivation

options.label: New `review` status mapped to the Review column
options.description: Non-terminal pause; `persist` maps `review → review`; `deriveRunStatus` returns `review` when a gate is pending and nothing is active/blocked.
options.consequence: Touches every `Record<PipelineRunStatus, …>` (compiler catches), the sanitizer whitelist, CLI/TUI labels and the card's Done guard; gives the exact Review card with no amber.

options.label: A new `human-step` block kind under `blocked`
options.description: Reuse the block machinery and Retry/Advance UI.
options.consequence: Card is amber and labelled Blocked, which contradicts "same as Review"; the block/retry state machine grows a kind that is not a failure.

options.label: Keep `running` with a paused flag
options.description: No new status; `humanSteps` on the run state says it is waiting.
options.consequence: Card stays Running with Stop visible; Review-column behavior would have to be special-cased in the card; every status consumer sees a lying "running".

recommendation.reason: It is the only representation that makes the card's Review behavior and the non-terminal pause true at the same time.

questions.title: If one branch reaches a human step while other branches are still running, what pauses?
questions.why: Decides whether the run status flips to Review immediately, waits for siblings, or holds all further launches. It also decides whether a gate can be acted on while siblings run.
questions.context: `transition:"all"` fans out; `run.active` holds several executions. `deriveRunStatus` returns `running` whenever `run.active` is non-empty. A gate has no step task and no agent. The goal says the pipeline "pauses" at the gate; with fan-out, "the pipeline" and "that branch" differ.

evidence.label: active executions drive the status

options.label: Pause only that branch
options.description: The gate is actionable as soon as it arrives. Other branches keep running and may launch further steps. The run stays `running` until every live execution settles, then `review` if a gate is still pending. Multiple gates may be pending; each is independent.
options.consequence: Smallest change; matches the existing `run.active`/`deriveRunStatus` model. The card is Running (Stop visible) while siblings work, and Review once they settle; the gate is opened from the run view in the meantime.

options.label: Hold the whole pipeline
options.description: Once any gate is pending, no branch launches another step; agents already running finish (they cannot be paused), then the run becomes `review`. The gate is actionable immediately.
options.consequence: A true breaker, but needs a run-level hold for every pending launch (like the stopped-run holds), plus tests for joins/retries; materially larger.

options.label: Flip the run to `review` immediately, siblings keep running
options.description: The moment a gate arrives the status/column is review; live siblings continue in the background.
options.consequence: Card says Review while agents are still writing to the worktree; the human may accept/return into live work; `deriveRunStatus` and every "review means idle" assumption change.

recommendation.reason: The runner cannot pause a live agent anyway; branch-only reuses `run.active` and `deriveRunStatus` without inventing a run-level hold.

questions.title: When the human accepts and the gate has more than one outgoing edge, how is the next step chosen?
questions.why: Decides whether the panel needs a target picker and whether `transition` remains meaningful on a human step.
questions.context: `resolveNextSteps` already implements the agent rules: `transition:"all"` launches every outgoing step; otherwise zero outgoing is terminal, one is taken, and several are matched against the handoff's `next`. A human emits no handoff with a `next` field unless the panel asks.

evidence.label: the existing resolver

options.label: Reuse the step's `transition`
options.description: `choose` → the panel lists the outgoing steps and the human picks one; `all` → Accept launches every outgoing step; zero outgoing → Accept finishes the run.
options.consequence: One resolver for agents and humans; the editor keeps `transition`; the panel's target picker is conditional.

options.label: Always make the human pick one
options.description: Ignore `transition`; Accept requires selecting exactly one outgoing step (or finishing when there are none).
options.consequence: Simpler panel, but `transition` becomes a dead field on human steps and a fan-out gate cannot accept all at once.

options.label: Always launch every outgoing step
options.description: No target picker; Accept fans out to all outgoing steps, or finishes when there are none.
options.consequence: Simplest runtime, but a gate with two alternative paths cannot choose one.

recommendation.reason: The resolver, editor field and tests already exist; only the panel's picker is new.

sections.title: Return mechanics
sections.intro: These decide what "send it back to the previous step" actually does, and how the loop is guaranteed to come back to the same gate.

questions.title: What does "return to the previous step" do mechanically?
questions.why: The two implementations touch different subsystems and have different context/risk profiles.
questions.context: The previous step's task is already `done`. (a) A fresh execution reuses `launchStep` (new hidden task, new `seq`, new session, the step's normal handoff contract) and can carry the human comment + its prior handoff in `composeStepPrompt`. (b) `sendInput` into the existing task session preserves the conversation but needs the execution re-armed in `run.active`, a settle path for the new turn, and a handoff-contract reminder; the runner's settle/lookback/held logic is the most intricate part of this subsystem.

evidence.label: the prompt composer already takes prior handoffs
launchStep is the existing launch path

options.label: Fresh execution of the previous step
options.description: New step task/session, new `seq`, same frozen profile and shared worktree; the prompt contains the human comment (trusted) and the handoff the human reviewed (untrusted).
options.consequence: Reuses `launchStep`/`composeStepPrompt`; the agent loses its session memory but keeps the transcript in history; lowest risk.

options.label: Send the comment into the previous step's existing session
options.description: Re-arm the settled execution, send the comment as a follow-up turn, remind it of the handoff contract.
options.consequence: Preserves context, but touches `sendInput`, the settle/lookback window, held/background-agent state and re-open semantics; needs a spike first.

options.label: Offer both, per gate
options.description: A toggle in the panel: fresh run vs continue the old session.
options.consequence: Two paths to build, test and document; the CLI needs the same toggle.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option that reuses the existing launch path end to end and guarantees the step ends with a handoff; resume is a separate feature.

questions.title: After a Return, must the same agent step always come back to this gate, even if its normal handoff rules would send it elsewhere?
questions.why: Without an answer, a returned step with several outgoing edges can choose a different branch and the human never sees the fix. This is the review loop's core guarantee.
questions.context: When any execution settles, `advanceOnHandoff` calls `resolveNextSteps` on the step's outgoing edges. For `transition:"choose"` with several edges, the agent's new `<handoff>.next` decides the target; nothing forces it back to the gate. The human comment could be followed by the agent answering a different branch.

evidence.label: settle resolves the step's outgoing edges
evidence.code: async function advanceOnHandoff(input: { ...; handoff: Handoff; resolved: { kind: "terminal" } | { kind: "steps"; stepIds: string[] }; }) { ... }

evidence.label: next is chosen by the handoff

options.label: Record the return target on the execution and force that edge on settle
options.description: The returned execution remembers `returnToStepId`; when it settles, the resolver takes that edge regardless of `transition`/`next`. Other outgoing edges of that execution are not launched.
options.consequence: Guarantees the loop; adds one optional field to the history record and a branch in `advanceOnHandoff`; a fan-out step's other branches are not re-run by this execution.

options.label: Only tell the agent in the prompt to choose the reviewing step
options.description: Add "end by handing off to <gate>" to the prompt; enforcement stays with the model.
options.consequence: No runtime change, but a model can ignore it and the gate is silently skipped; the e2e cannot assert the guarantee.

options.label: Require the returned-to step's only outgoing edge to be the gate
options.description: Validate that an agent step feeding a human step has exactly one outgoing edge.
options.consequence: Structural guarantee, but forbids a gate after a fan-out step and rejects graphs the editor can draw today.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option that makes the review loop deterministic without restricting the graph.

questions.title: May a human step have more than one incoming edge?
questions.why: Multiple incoming turns the gate into a join: wait for every source, show several handoffs, and Return needs a target. Single incoming makes Return unambiguous and removes a whole join/arrival path.
questions.context: The goal says the gate is added "between two steps, and at the end". The existing model supports `join:"all"` fan-in with `run.joins` and `PipelineJoinArrival {fromStepId, seq, handoff}`. A human gate has no task; its pending state must hold arrivals itself. Even with one incoming, an Accept to a join step still needs the human comment carried with the arrival, so the arrival contract changes either way.

evidence.label: the arrival shape
join state on the run
evidence.code: joins: Record<string, { arrivals: PipelineJoinArrival[] }>;

options.label: Exactly one incoming edge
options.description: The gate is inserted on one edge (or at the end). Return always targets that source; no join wait; no arrival picker. A branch that needs its own review gets its own gate.
options.consequence: Validation + editor reject >1 incoming; simplest state and UI; a fan-in gate is not possible in v1.

options.label: Multiple incoming, forced `join:"all"`
options.description: Wait for every distinct source, show every arrival's handoff, and require a Return target when there are several (default latest).
options.consequence: Reuses `run.joins` but adds human arrivals, a return-target picker and more e2e; supports fan-in review.

recommendation.reason: The request describes an edge insertion ("between two steps"), and one incoming removes the join/return-target branch from both the runner and the panel.

sections.title: Control panel
sections.intro: These decide what the owner sees and can press while the gate is pending.

questions.title: What form does the human control panel take, and where is it opened?
questions.why: Decides component placement, navigation and whether the panel can coexist with the run view's existing side panel.
questions.context: `PipelineRunView` already has a right-hand side panel with Goal, blocked entries, `reviewActive` and history. A human gate would be a new section or a separate overlay. Entry points available: the human node on the canvas, a run-view Review button, and the board card's Review action (Q1). The app's view union is `board | pipelines | pipeline-run`.

evidence.label: existing side panel

options.label: A modal/drawer over the run view
options.description: Opened from the human node, a run-view **Review** button, and the card's Review action. No auto-open on arrival; the node highlights and a notification fires. Closing keeps the gate pending; a half-typed comment stays while the run view is open.
options.consequence: New component + modal state; room for history + form; the existing side panel is untouched.

options.label: A section in the existing run-view side panel
options.description: Clicking the human node selects it and the side panel shows the gate form instead of/in addition to the history.
options.consequence: No overlay, but cramped with history + handoff + comment; the card action has to open the run view and select the node.

options.label: A full-page review route
options.description: A dedicated `pipeline-review` view.
options.consequence: Most room, but a new view/navigation path and overkill for a single form.

recommendation.reason: The panel must show a handoff, history and a form; the run view's side panel is already dense, and a modal can be opened from both the canvas and the card.

questions.title: What must the human panel show?
questions.why: Each item is UI + data wiring; the diff in particular adds a call and a dialog.
questions.context: The run has `run.history` (outcomes, handoffs), the gate's arrival handoff (the last handoff), the frozen graph (goal/step instructions), the parent task (worktree) and step tasks (transcripts). `DiffDialog` already exists at App level and is opened with a `Task`; the run view does not currently receive an `onShowDiff`.

evidence.label: the dialog already exists
evidence.code:
<DiffDialog
  open={!!diffTask}
  task={diffTask ? (tasks.find((t) => t.id === diffTask.id) ?? diffTask) : null}
  onClose={() => setDiffTask(null)}
/>

evidence.label: history entries carry handoffs

options.label: Pipeline goal
options.description: The frozen goal text.

options.label: The human step's "What to check" instructions
options.description: The step's `instructions` field, read-only; never sent to an agent.

options.label: The last handoff (the arrival from the previous step)
options.description: Rendered with the existing `HandoffCard`.

options.label: The run's history
options.description: Every step's name, outcome and handoff, including prior human decisions.

options.label: Links to each completed step's transcript
options.description: Opens the step task/transcript.

options.label: Prior human decisions on this gate
options.description: The comments and Accept/Return outcomes from earlier rounds, so the reviewer sees what they asked for last time.

options.label: A "View changes" button for the shared worktree diff
options.description: Reuses the App-level `DiffDialog` against the parent task.

recommendation.reason: The gate's purpose is to judge the work; the diff and prior rounds are the two things the old side panel cannot show.

questions.title: Which run-level actions stay available while a human gate is pending?
questions.why: The run is not `running`, so Stop currently 409s; Restart isn't offered for `review` yet. Leaving no escape hatch strands the run.
questions.context: `cancelPipelineRun` only acts when something is live or a runner decision is pending. `RESTARTABLE_STATUSES` is `done|cancelled|blocked`. Retry/Advance/Done are meaningless for a gate with no task. Archive/delete already exist.

evidence.label: restart gate
evidence.code: const RESTARTABLE_STATUSES: PipelineRunStatus[] = ["done", "cancelled", "blocked"];

evidence.label: cancel only acts on live work

options.label: Restart only (confirm clears history)
options.description: The run view's Restart button becomes available for `review`; Stop/Retry/Advance/Done are hidden. Archive/delete remain.
options.consequence: One escape hatch; no new cancel path; restarting discards the review state and history after the existing confirm.

options.label: Restart + Stop (cancel the run, keep history)
options.description: Stop cancels the run, dismisses the gate and moves the card to Ready, preserving the audit trail.
options.consequence: New no-live cancel path + tests; gives "abandon without restarting".

options.label: No run-level action
options.description: Only archive/delete.
options.consequence: Abandoning the run removes it from the board; a wrong gate cannot be cancelled in place.

recommendation.reason: Restart is the existing escape hatch and already confirms history loss; adding a no-live cancel path is extra lifecycle for an action Return/archive already cover.

sections.title: CLI & bundle contract
sections.intro: The two surfaces outside the webview that need an explicit decision.

questions.title: How much CLI support does the human step need?
questions.why: Decides a route + client method + command + tests, and whether a headless user can clear a gate.
questions.context: Pipeline run-control routes are `app+cli`; the CLI already has `show`, `status`, `advance`, `retry`, `restart`. `pipeline status` currently does `h.taskId.slice(0, 8)` and would crash on a human history record with `taskId: null`, so `show`/`status` need a fix regardless.

evidence.label: the crash

options.label: Full parity: `agetor pipeline review <ref> --accept|--return --comment …`
options.description: Plus `--next <step>` for choose, and human-step display in `show`/`status`; tests.
options.consequence: Matches the repo's convention and lets a headless user clear a gate; more surface.

options.label: Read-only: show/status display the gate, decisions only in the UI
options.description: Fix the nullable `taskId` crash and print the pending gate.
options.consequence: Smaller; a headless user cannot accept/return.

options.label: UI only
options.description: Only fix the crash; no gate display.
options.consequence: CLI shows a paused run with no explanation; worst parity.

recommendation.reason: Every other pipeline action is available from both the app and the CLI; a gate that only the webview can clear breaks that contract.

questions.title: How should a human step travel in an exported bundle?
questions.why: The bundle is a versioned file format shared between app versions; old readers drop unknown step fields.
questions.context: `BundleStep` is `{id,name,instructions,agent,position,subagents,transition,join}`; export builds those fields explicitly, import maps `agent`→`agentProfileId` and spreads `...rest` before validation. `BUNDLE_VERSION` is 1 and readers refuse `version > 1`. The documented convention is that additive fields keep version 1 and old exports stay byte-identical. An old reader that drops `type` sees an agent step with `agent: null`; `createTask` then refuses to run it ("step has no agent").

evidence.label: the step shape
readers reject a newer version
additive fields keep version 1
evidence.code: `speed` is written as `speed !== "off"` so an older agetor still imports the Agent ... and the format stays version 1

options.label: Keep version 1, add `type:"human"` only for human steps
options.description: Agent steps write no `type`, so old exports stay byte-identical.
options.consequence: Old readers import a pipeline with a broken step (recoverable in the editor) instead of refusing the file; no version logic.

options.label: Write version 2 only when the bundle contains a human step
options.description: Human-free bundles stay v1; the parser accepts 1 and 2.
options.consequence: Old readers refuse the file with "update agetor"; more version-selection + parser tests; departs from the additive-v1 convention.

options.label: Bump every export to version 2
options.description: The parser accepts 1 and 2.
options.consequence: Safest for old readers but every new bundle is rejected by every old app, even human-free ones.

recommendation.reason: The bundle doc explicitly keeps version 1 for additive fields; the old reader fails at run time with a clear "step has no agent" and the new import preview can show the human step.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I would bet on. One click each; override only if you disagree.

questions.title: Human-step graph rules: never the start step; at least one incoming (exactly one per Q7); no agent or subagents; no human→human edges; allowed at the end (terminal Accept finishes).

recommendation.value: All enforced in `validatePipelineGraph` and the editor; a human step saves with `agentProfileId: null`, empty subagents, and no start/Set-as-start affordance.
recommendation.reason: These keep `resolveStartStep`, `createTask`/`buildSnapshot` and the runner's agent requirement intact.

questions.title: Comments: trimmed; a non-blank comment is required for Return; optional for Accept; max 8,000 characters (`PIPELINE_LIMITS.handoffField`); a terminal Accept needs none.

recommendation.value: As stated; blank/whitespace Return is rejected by the route and disabled in the UI; Accept with a blank comment is allowed.
recommendation.reason: Reuses the existing handoff-field cap and matches the request's "necessary/optional" wording.

questions.title: Human comments are trusted: rendered as a separate `## Human review feedback` section outside the untrusted-handoff markers; agent handoffs stay fenced; the comment must survive a blocked/retried Accept/Return.

recommendation.value: Yes — a dedicated trusted section, stored on the human history record and carried on the pending launch/arrival, never folded into a `Handoff` that `composeStepPrompt` fences.
recommendation.reason: The trust model says agent handoffs are untrusted and owner comments are trusted; fencing a comment would mislabel it, and prompt-only storage would lose it on Retry.

questions.title: Human gate entries do **not** count toward `maxSteps`.

recommendation.value: They are recorded in `history` and shown in progress, but do not increment `stepCount`; entering a gate is never blocked by the step cap.
recommendation.reason: A gate spends no agent budget, and a run that cannot reach its reviewer because of a cap is a dead end; the Return re-run of the previous agent step still counts and bounds the loop.

questions.title: Human step visual: an info-tinted border + a "Human" chip + a user-check icon; no "No agent" warning; no amber attention ring.

recommendation.value: As stated; the pending gate uses the same info highlight on the canvas and in the panel header; the run status chip reads "Review".
recommendation.reason: It must read as a different element without borrowing the warning color that means "Blocked".

questions.title: Editor: add a "Human step" choice to Add step and a type switch in the step panel; insertion between two steps uses the existing Add step + Connect to… flow (no new one-click edge split); a human step cannot be Set as start.

recommendation.value: As stated; switching an agent step to human clears its agent/subagents; switching back to agent starts unbound; `deleteStep` never promotes a human step to start.
recommendation.reason: Keeps the editor change small; the graph constraints make a human start invalid anyway.

questions.title: The panel has exactly two decisions — Return and Accept; no separate Reject/Stop/Escalate.

recommendation.value: Accept follows the outgoing edges and only finishes when there are none; Return loops with a required comment; abandoning the run stays Restart/archive/delete.
recommendation.reason: Matches the request exactly; a third action would need its own state and prompt semantics.

questions.title: Manual Advance may target a human step; it enters the gate with `handoff: null`, and Return targets the step it was advanced from.

recommendation.value: As stated; the panel shows "no handoff" for that arrival; the gate is otherwise identical.
recommendation.reason: The existing Advance form lists every step; silently excluding human steps would be a surprising hole.

questions.title: On entering a human gate: one "Pipeline needs your review" toast/OS notification per gate; no "Pipeline finished" until a terminal Accept.

recommendation.value: As stated; the notification is deduped per run+gate seq; clicking it opens the run view with the gate selected; the status chip still reads "Review".
recommendation.reason: A headless-core user must learn the run is waiting; "Pipeline finished" would be a lie while a gate is pending.

questions.title: Do you have a mock, screenshot, PRD or ticket for the panel or the human node that is not in the repo?
questions.why: Matching your intended panel layout or node treatment saves a round of rework.
